keyVerseText: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part , maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love.
rootMeaning: The word ἐπιχορηγία (epichorēgía) derives from the verb ἐπιχορηγέω (epichorēgéō), which means to add, minister nourishment, or fully supply. This root conveys the idea of providing something additional or supplementary, going beyond mere provision to actively aid or contribute. Unlike the simple English term 'supply,' the Greek root emphasizes an intentional and effective furnishing, highlighting both the source and the beneficial purpose of the provision.
usageInScripture: This noun appears twice in the New Testament and is translated primarily as 'supplieth' and 'the supply.' Both translations reflect the essential idea of providing what is needed to sustain or build up. The consistency in translation suggests a focus on the functional aspect of supply—something that actively supports or strengthens, rather than a passive or incidental provision. This usage underscores the word's role in describing contributions that are vital and purposeful within the community of believers.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐπιχορηγία enriches our grasp of how God equips the church and believers. It points to the divine provision that is not merely adequate but abundant and enabling, ensuring the body of Christ functions harmoniously and grows. This concept aligns with the biblical teaching that every member contributes uniquely and indispensably to the church's spiritual health and maturity. Recognizing this word's meaning encourages believers to value both the giving and receiving aspects of ministry as vital to the edification of the whole body in love.
keyVerseReflection: Ephesians 4:16 speaks of the whole body being joined and compacted by what every joint 'supplieth,' highlighting the active role of each part in the church's growth. The use of ἐπιχορηγία here emphasizes that each member's contribution is not incidental but effectual and purposeful, working according to the measure of each part's capacity. This supply is what fosters increase and edification, demonstrating that the church thrives through the intentional and nourishing provision of its members, unified in love.
